title: Monsoon and Current
premise: Jude Vasquez, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Marrow Fund's smiling enforcers, chases a freak tide into a sea cave that coastal legend says holds the drowned fortune of a smuggler hanged for a crime he didn't commit. Inside she finds not gold but a ledger proving the hanging was orchestrated by the Fund's founder — and a dying old man who makes her promise to carry the truth over the mountains before the first snow seals the pass. Pursued by the Fund's collectors and shadowed by Elias, a Fund auditor who begins to doubt his own employer, Jude must choose between selling the ledger to erase her debt and delivering justice the law abandoned eighty years ago. She crosses the range in the season's first blizzard, loses the money but keeps the truth, and ends the book testifying at a hearing that finally clears the smuggler's name — walking away free, broke, and no longer running.
about_author: Ulyana Fairweather is the pen name of a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade documenting shipwreck folklore along the northern coast. She writes adventure novels from a converted fishing trawler, where she claims the best plots arrive with the fog.

chapters.title: The Debt of Good Weather
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Chasing a storm for footage she can sell, Jude calculates she's three payments from the Marrow Fund taking her truck, her gear, her freedom of movement. A collector named Brannic delivers a friendly ultimatum. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of a woman whose whole life is momentum.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. An unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave the locals refuse to name. Inside she finds the skeleton of the hanged smuggler, a weatherproof ledger, and Old Tam, a hermit keeper of the cave, mid-heart-attack. His dying request: carry the ledger over Corren Pass before snowfall. Beat: reluctant inheritance.

chapters.title: Names in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with a flashback to the smuggler's era. Reading the ledger by lamplight, Jude discovers the Fund's founder built his fortune on the smuggler's betrayed cargo and bought the hanging. The names connect to Brannic's chain of command. Beat: the debt she owes becomes a debt owed to her.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Everything
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A Fund auditor sent to recover the cave's contents, Elias reconstructs Jude's route with unsettling precision — and finds an anomaly in the Fund's own archives that matches the ledger's dates. Beat: the hunter's first crack of doubt.

chapters.title: Foothold Town
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the last town before the pass, Jude tries to sell the ledger to a journalist, who warns her the Fund owns the courthouse too. Brannic's collectors arrive; a chase through the fish market ends with Jude's truck burned. Beat: no more running by road.

chapters.title: Two Travelers, One Pass
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Elias catches Jude at the trailhead — and instead of seizing the ledger, asks to read it. His arithmetic doesn't lie: the Fund murdered a man. They strike a wary bargain to cross together. Beat: enemies becoming something unnameable, trust as risk.

chapters.title: The Range Before the Snows
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The climb: a rope bridge fails, Elias nearly dies saving the ledger, and in a shelter cave they speak honestly — her debts, his complicity, the smuggler's daughter the ledger records. Beat: love admitted aloud in the one place neither can flee.

chapters.title: White Silence
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The blizzard hits early. Brannic's team, flown in by helicopter, traps them above the tree line. Elias offers himself and a forged confession in exchange for Jude's passage; Brannic takes the deal and leaves Elias bleeding in the snow. Beat: sacrifice, and the terror of being the one left walking.

chapters.title: The Other Side of the Mountain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Half-frozen, Jude reaches the valley and finds Elias alive, cached in a shepherd's hut by the very smuggler's descendants the ledger names. Together they reach the provincial archive before it closes for winter and file the ledger into the record. Beat: justice begins as paperwork done in a blizzard.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Spring: the hearing clears the smuggler's name; the Fund's founder's estate is unraveled. Jude's debt is voided as an illegal instrument, Brannic turns state's evidence, and Elias resigns. On the coast, the tide opens the cave again and they return the ledger to the sea. Beat: stillness chosen, not forced — the end of running.
